name: Smart Home and Home Technology
purpose: AhernAI sales discovery and illustrative configuration guidance
summary: For smart-home, audiovisual and home-network installers. Clarify technology installation versus mains electrical work. Explore consultations, project intake and ordinary support coordination. Ask one useful question at a time about the caller's actual workflow. Explain Level 1 when messages and FAQs fit; move directly to Level 2 when the caller needs routine work completed. Recommend the lowest suitable level as soon as the need is understood; no mandatory three-level tour. Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.
discovery_questions: Do you mainly install smart-home systems, home theaters and networks, or also perform electrical work?
Are most calls new projects, help with existing installations, or scheduling questions?
What happens to calls when your technicians are in a customer's home?
Which approved equipment and service-area questions do you answer repeatedly?
Would a detailed callback request solve the problem, or should callers arrange a consultation?
Which situations need the owner or a senior technician, and what system holds that information?

levels.name: Answering Service
use_cases: Answer approved service-area and installation-category FAQs without asserting unverified device compatibility.
Capture contact details, general project type, property location and whether the caller is an existing customer.
Record a plain-language support concern and send a callback summary to one agreed destination.
levels.probe: When you finish an installation, would one organized summary give you enough to return the right calls?
fit_signals: Technicians need reliable message capture while onsite.
The team prefers to assess projects and schedule callbacks itself.

levels.name: Receptionist
use_cases: Qualify project categories, service area and desired timing, and offer screened transfers to the appropriate human.
Book or reschedule approved consultations and update the agreed project or customer system through the included receptionist automation.
Capture ordinary support requests, share approved status information from authorized sources and route issues to the agreed technician queue.
levels.probe: What should happen between a project inquiry and a confirmed consultation?
fit_signals: The caller needs routine receptionist work completed rather than only a message.
Approved business rules and verified systems support the agreed workflow.

levels.name: Manager
use_cases: Collect installation complaints, affected equipment categories and the requested resolution for human review.
Explain approved support or warranty policies and route disputed coverage or exceptions to the responsible person.

Support approved employee coordination, such as recording a shift callout or coverage request and routing it to the authorized supervisor. Employment, staffing approval, disciplinary, financial and policy-exception decisions remain human; do not request medical reasons or other sensitive employee details.
levels.probe: Only after the caller raises a management need: Which situations should the agent handle under approved rules, and which should reach you?
fit_signals: The caller asks for help with difficult or disgruntled callers and escalations.
The caller wants approved employee coordination or supervisory support.

scope_boundaries: Do not collect Wi-Fi passwords, lock or alarm codes, private camera access, access tokens or security bypass instructions.
Do not provide electrical repair, wiring, bypass or hazardous troubleshooting instructions; use approved human escalation paths.
Do not guarantee device compatibility, network performance, remote repair, arrival times or coverage without approved facts.

Refunds, credits, financial commitments and policy exceptions remain human decisions. Texting and additional transfer usage charges retain their separately disclosed terms; included receptionist automation is not a separate build fee.

Level 1 captures approved FAQs, caller details and a summary to one destination; it does not book, submit orders, update a CRM or make screened transfers. Level 2 covers agreed routine receptionist duties and supporting automation. Package fit is based on duties, not a one-calendar/one-CRM or two-integration quota. Scope is agreed before launch; this is not an unlimited software-development commitment.

Routine receptionist duties and the supporting automation are included in the agreed Level 2 scope, without an additional AhernAI automation or integration-build charge. Confirm software compatibility, access, allowed actions and failure handling during setup; an unverified connection is not an automatic surcharge.

Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.

Do not promise that a named app or POS is supported merely because the caller names it. Verify compatibility during setup and agree a workable destination or fallback; disclose any actual work outside the agreed duties before proceeding.
setup_requirements: Confirm service categories, service area, business hours and the distinction between technology and electrical services.
Supply approved device/support FAQs, intake fields, information to avoid collecting and the summary destination.
Define appointment types or CRM fields, qualification rules, screened transfer contacts and escalation fallbacks.
Provide approved warranty language and complaint handling rules; confirm integration compatibility and test representative calls.
Agree the routine duties and supporting automation included in the package, approved actions, access permissions, successful completion signals and failure paths before launch.

adjacent_services.trigger: Prospects cannot understand installation options online.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a clear service page and project inquiry form.

adjacent_services.trigger: The business needs broader back-office work beyond its agreed receptionist duties.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a separate project only for that broader need. Automation needed for agreed Level 2 receptionist work is already included; do not resell it as a Quickstart or add-on.

adjacent_services.trigger: The business needs help with its own network infrastructure.
adjacent_services.example: Discuss an assessment and written scope rather than promising a partnership or subcontracting arrangement.
